acceptedRecordSnapshot.RequiredArtifact: Versioned secret custody for Provider credentials, per-tenant KEKs and DigestKeys, tenant migration-epoch/directory-effect capability signing keys with exact revocation state, the reserved-system security-observation digest key, per-export envelope keys, manifest-signing keys/public trust anchors, trusted-envelope HMAC keys, and decision-authority verification anchors/trust profile. Decision-approval signing keys remain outside Agents and platform-host custody under the independently governed issuer named by that profile; the profile binds issuer, stable actor/authority-role sources for Product, Governance, Security, Architecture, and named maintainers, key-use purpose, freshness/expiry/revocation, and forbids the Release Operator recorder or platform key custodian from requesting or minting approval evidence. The trusted-envelope profile fixes issuer/audience, numeric maximum tag lifetime, clock skew, rotation overlap, command retry/recovery horizon, and `ReplayRecordRetention` no shorter than the greater of tag lifetime plus skew plus overlap and that recovery horizon, consumed by the Agents-owned reserved-`system` `TrustedEnvelopeReplay(Issuer, DeliveryNonce)` aggregate whose record binds the authenticated target tenant; it also fixes active/revoked key state, emergency revocation, retained digest-key versions, decision-manifest verification, wrap/unwrap/pin/unpin/destroy operations with irreversible receipts, safe rotation/invalidation signals, and a principal-bound `DeliverExportKey(DeliveryId, ExportId, CommitAcknowledgementRevision, RequesterActorId, Purpose, Audience, ExclusiveExpiry, LifecycleVersion, StoreTarget, ContractVersion)` operation whose key bytes are delivered directly to that authenticated principal. Delivery is idempotent by the complete identity and exposes authenticated exact outcome lookup as `Delivered(ObservedAt)`, `NotDelivered(Reason)`, or `Unknown/Unavailable`; the custodian rejects cross-tenant, changed-identity, expired, or revoked authority before release. Only opaque references, versions, public anchors, policy bounds, and configured/not-configured state cross Agents boundaries.

acceptedRecordSnapshot.RequiredArtifact: Platform-owned host composition for the Agents DomainService and UI with EventStore, Conversations, Parties, Tenants, Provider and safety adapters, Dapr Workflow, secrets, health, identity, telemetry, and a replicated durable content-free `security-audit-spool`. The spool accepts a deterministic `SecurityObservationId` before a classified Agents denial returns, retains pending records across EventStore/replay outages, exposes exact-id outcome lookup/acknowledgement, and grants its drain worker an ACL restricted to the computed `SecurityEventLog(RoutingTenantId, UtcDay)` stream and event; if the spool itself is unavailable, ingress constructs no Agents command and platform health blocks tenant-access/audit readiness. The host additionally binds the production `EXT-PROTECTION-1` engine and exposes the FR-34 attestation port used at startup and every readiness evaluation. The port lets Agents seal a canary, prove persisted bytes contain no plaintext, unseal it, destroy its DEK, replay `Erased`, and obtain engine identity/version for comparison with the committed protection target; the host fails closed against both the no-op default and a self-reporting wrapper around it. For Story 6.1 it also composes the target-limited directory-migration Workflow and EventStore namespace ports. Installing a tenant migration epoch revokes the legacy direct-write credential/epoch, and every later interaction/failure create or content append requires the current epoch plus an exact directory permit or committed-effect capability. Every `ConversationAgentState` permit, creation/workflow-start/User-action-intent outbox, lease acquire/commit, and interaction-owned rate/open/Budget/capacity phase-authorization append is likewise conditional on the current directory capability at EventStore. Repair first atomically installs a directory-repair fence that revokes all those new-directory/effect-authorization operations and returns an authenticated checkpoint; only the post-fence finite permit/outbox/lease/phase-authorization cohort may enter the old-epoch bridge, whose exact pending/committed/authorized work drains before successor activation revokes the old epoch, repair fence, and bridge. For Story 8.3 the same port evaluates canonical `GovernanceScopeV1` and its predicate digest from authoritative tenant stream identity, immutable first-event/directory-permit `SourceConversationId`, and permit/action/lease/phase-authorization owner facts—never caller classification. Before either deletion origin builds a candidate, it conditionally installs a persistent ordinal scope admission fence that rejects later matching permit, User-action-intent, lease-acquire/commit, and rate/open/Budget/capacity phase-authorization appends; after the finite same-ordinal owner cycles become Effective it conditionally installs and verifies the separate content write fence that rejects later matching interaction/failure creates or content appends. The admission violation ledger is one append-only request ledger partitioned by fence ordinal: prior violations remain visible, while only the current installed ordinal can attest `ZeroAcceptedViolationsSinceInstall`. A pre-cut violation uses an explicit no-global-cut/candidate/token receipt; a later violation invalidates only exact present artifacts. Both assign one successor ordinal and require separately keyed owner cycles carrying all prior obligations. The content guard is stable by request/predicate and continuously installed: after one or more recuts, a successor-binding authorize/effect/result operation starts from the latest installed binding and appends the new ordinal/global-cut/token only after proving a complete gap-free ordered chain of intervening invalidated/tokenless ordinal receipts and the current zero proof; an overtaken authorization returns terminal obsolete without a guard append. The port also owns the tenant `GovernanceScopeGuard`: every authorized legal-hold request conditionally registers its canonical scope there before fence preparation and remains until an exact fully acknowledged release removes it. Hold registration and `CommitDeletionDestructionStartBarrierEffect` serialize on that owner. The `ProtectionFence` barrier authorization persists the exact observed `GovernanceScopeGuard` revision/compare token. Conditional append at that revision makes the seal operation serialize with admission writes and hold registration/release; an intervening mutation returns authenticated stale and must be mirrored before revision-bound reauthorization. The seal operation verifies both ledgers/current content binding/migration receipts, rejects any overlapping contender that won after authorization unless it consumes the exact effective deletion-allowed hold disposition, commits immutable `DestructionSealed`, and returns one deterministic non-expiring, revocable, single-use `DestroyDekManifest` capability bound to the sorted accepted key-target manifest; it has no `ExpiresAt` or renewal branch, and its capability-key version remains verifiable through outage, migration, restore, and the full retention of the batch identity and terminal outcome, including exact retry/lookup after consumption or revocation. No direct clean read, stale no-hold authorization, or unrelated append is authority. Each fence/guard/barrier exposes authenticated installation, exact-outcome lookup, verification/high-water, and complete append-only evidence; every admission ordinal/violation gap chain, owner cycle, content binding, hold contender/release, barrier/containment compare authorization and stale result, destruction seal, and batch identity/capability-key/guard-issued state plus referenced protection-owner blocked, reserved, re-attested, consumed, or revoked outcome survives migration successors. The protection engine consumes each manifest batch atomically as all targets or none, returns an ordered per-target irreversible receipt vector, and exposes exact batch lookup; each first previously uncovered complete protection target from an authoritative post-seal content violation is ProtectionFence-serialized into one monotonic ordinal and immutable singleton target manifest, while later same-target resources receive coverage links only, then follows `AuthorizeDeletionContainmentBatch`, guard-revision-conditional `CommitDeletionContainmentBatchEffect`, exact lookup, and `RecordDeletionContainmentBatchIssued` or `RecordDeletionContainmentBatchIssuanceStale` before its distinct batch may be consumed; exact duplicates reuse the ordinal/result and concurrent distinct targets receive distinct ordinals. An accepted admission after sealing invokes `BlockDeletionBatchConsumption` to race `ReserveAndConsumeDeletionBatch` at the protection owner, records `DeletionIntegrityCompromised`, blocks new batches, and can never be treated as resource-only content containment or successful completion. Missing, malformed, unknown-version, cross-tenant, or unverifiable scope membership rejects a write and prevents a clean verification result. The artifact replaces module-owned AppHost, Aspire, and ServiceDefaults ownership.

acceptedRecordSnapshot.RequiredArtifact: A production payload-protection engine behind the existing EventStore hooks, applied field-level to a `ProtectedContent` envelope so every other event field stays plaintext and a destroyed-key field unprotects as the typed value `Erased` without breaking replay: one data-encryption key per `AgentInteraction`, plus an explicit provider-neutral `TargetProtectionKeyAlias` that lets a target-limited creation-outbox `ProtectedContent` field owned by `ConversationAgentState` select that exact interaction DEK without deriving it from the directory aggregate identity, wrapped by a per-tenant key-encryption key custodied through `EXT-SECRETS-1`. The custodian exposes `WrapDek`, `UnwrapDek`, `PinDek`, `UnpinDek`, per-key `DestroyDek`, and an atomic `DestroyDekManifest(BatchId, ManifestDigest, SortedTenantInteractionAliasTargets, GuardCapability)` operation. The batch identity and signed capability are deterministic and target-bound. The capability is non-expiring and revocable, carries its signing-key version, and that version remains verifiable for the full retention of the batch identity and terminal outcome, including exact retry/lookup after consumption or revocation; there is no expiry or renewal path and restore reuses the same identity. Consumption is single-use and all-or-none, returns an ordered irreversible per-target receipt vector, exact retry/lookup returns that vector, a changed target/digest conflicts, and `BlockDeletionBatchConsumption` races `ReserveAndConsumeDeletionBatch` at the same protection owner so exactly one wins. Each first previously uncovered complete protection target `(TenantId, AgentInteractionId, TargetProtectionKeyAlias)` uses one guard-issued batch for its ProtectionFence-assigned monotonic containment ordinal and immutable singleton target manifest; later violation resources for that same target receive coverage links only, no ProtectionFence event alone is a guard capability, and distinct uncovered targets receive distinct ordinals/batches. Hold pinning rejects both per-key and manifest destruction; sealed envelopes remain sealed on broker/read models, `PayloadUnprotectionOutcome` is unreadable after erasure, and snapshot/replay caches inherit the DEK (AD-22, AD-27). The shipped no-op default is not acceptable for content-bearing workflows (AD-14).
